Not as good as the filters that came with the humidifier - I am not happy with these wicks. They do not hold together as well as the ones that came with the humidifier. They become very soft and sag down to the bottom of the humidifier, thus making the humidifier much less effective. They are also very fragile and despite handling them with great care when cleaning them, they end up frayed and torn, which also harms their effectiveness.

I ran my humidifier 24 hours a day over the winter, and wash the humidifier and wicks weekly. Definitely do not bleach these or put them in hot water. I was being lazy and wanted them clean fast, big mistake. That's how I destroyed the first set that came with the humidifier. They dissolve like wet toilet paper. Now I soak them in tepid water and a cup of distilled vinegar for a few hours until all of the minerals (brown-yellowish-pink buildup) and algae are gone, like what the instructions say. Daily when I refilled the reservoirs, I rotated these filters so that the dry and crusty part is down in the fresh water. This seems to keep them clean for a couple more days.

Frustrated with how flimsy and floppy these are, I tried an experiment. I bought one of the round Honeywell humidifier filters at my local big box mart. I cut it in half, and it fits in this Vornado humidifier. The Honeywell filters have some metal weaved in with the fibers, so they stand up. That's worked for the remainder of the winter, and they're still fine.

Saved Mom - My mother moved into a new place recently and discovered the fridge wasn't cooling at all. Being that it was late in the week, a tech wouldn't be able to look at it for a few days. Being that this was the first time my mother has moved in 20 years, she really needed a function fridge ASAP. After doing some research I found that this part commonly fails on the model of fridge my mother has (Kenmore 106.59422801). So I decided to tackle this issue on my own. I ordered this part and they relay which it was attached to. Since this is a overload/starting device, something must have cause the compressor to overload, killing the starting device. I could hear the relay clicking, but the compressor would not start. Upon further investigation I found the compressor fan blade had fallen off the motor in the bottom rear compartment, not sure how that happened but the motor was still spinning. After getting the fan back on the motor, I cleaned the coils that were completely blocked by dust build up. This further confirmed that we are definitely dealing with overloaded compressor. I installed the new start device and relay, plugged in the fridge and crossed my fingers. The compressor fired up instantly, 20 minutes later the fridge was cold again. "NAILED IT" Amazon got the part to me in a day, which I also have to extend my appreciation. If you have even the slightest bit of mechanical know how, you can do this yourself. If you can hook up a TV, you can replace this part. Very easy, plug-n-play install. The part is also very accessible from the back of the fridge.

REPLACE THEM ALL!!! - Really, just do it. The first time I repaired my dryer, I watched a YouTube video, did some Googling, ordered parts, marveled at all the excess parts, and fixed the dryer.

It dried one load of clothes. That was sad.

Looked inside and found that it had melted the end of the wire that goes from somewhere inside the dryer to the top heating element clip. Hmmm. It ends up that there's a secret they don't tell you - you have to replace BOTH the little parts on the element housing, even though only one of them tests bad. I was feeling too lazy to fix it again, so we called a repairman. He apparently didn't know the secret either, and it again dried one load of clothes. So I ordered the second set of parts, along with a "dryer heating element wire kit" to fix the by now seriously melted end of the wire.

I decided that I wasn't going to take any more chances, and I replaced ALL the parts. I even went so far as to cross reference the part numbers from the repair diagram to the Amazon numbers to make sure I had the correct parts. Ha! It works great now.

Basically, I can only use this thing on one cycle, normal. Anything other than normal and the drum bangs against the unit casing really loudly until it auto-retries to do a spin cycle, over and over and over. I’ve checked, and the unit is level... and the feet don’t wobble, so I’m not really sure what’s going on there.

It’s hard to judge, but I don’t really feel like it’s getting my clothes as clean either. I mean, for the most part it does the job, but occasionally you do have to wash something twice.

I’m not a big fan of how the cycles don’t remember when you make a change to something like water temp, etc. Normal defaults to warm, but I usually do either hot or cold. That said, I think there may be one cycle you can customize, but... with it banging so badly, I’m afraid to leave the normal cycle.

Now, I’m not saying Samsung is a better brand... my old washer almost caught fire when it finally broke (hence the switch to a new brand), but when it was working it was nicer than this machine.

Almost perfect - tricks to getting a better cup - The number one problem with K cups other than paying $60 per pound for coffee is that you either have to buy the variety packs and figure out what to do with that one version you really don't like, or you have to make a choice to buy a whole box of this or that or have multiple big boxes of brew laying about. Right now, I have 3 Costco size cases of various cups taking up about 4 cubic feet of my house.

So I got these very bright orange things with the idea that I could cut my coffee cost by 90% AND only buy the coffee I want without having to dedicate an entire closet to it.

I was a little concerned as they tend to look a bit flimsy. That however, is not a problem. I've used these now for several weeks and they are actually pretty sturdy. I figure I should be able to get a fair amount of wear out of them and the price wasn't hard to swallow either.

To use these takes a bit of a couple tricks, but nothing hard or time consuming, and once done, you set it and forget it. The first thing is to pull the Kcup holder out of the coffee pot. Open up the top, grab ahold of the holder, and just pull. It comes out and can easily go right back in.

Second, you may find your first cup leaks a bit, so try it first with just hot water. If so, open up the lid and pull down the O-ring just a hair or two. This seals the top of the place where the water goes in. Be careful though because the tip is just as sharp as it looks. Once pulled down, it will stay down unless you go back to the original Kcup, in which case you'll have to adjust it again. Simple!

Why orange? I don't know, but perhaps cheaper plastic? Or I'll suggest a more likely result of helping them not to be lost on a kitchen counter. Look around and these things will just pop right out at you.

It's a nice little invention and I think I'll include one for each of my Kcup drinking offspring at Christmas time.

Made in China. Make sure your expectations meet what the machine will do. - There are a plethora of the small ice machines being sold by Chinese companies on Amazon right now. One of the main differences between them is the number of cubes made at a time. This one makes twenty-four cubes at a time. A lot of the smaller machines make only nine cubes at a time.

This shows that this machine can make 40 pounds of ice in a twenty-four hour period. That’s a little bit misleading, because the only way it can do that is if you continuously remove the ice as it is being made. Once ice is made it goes into a basket and then it starts to melt. The water goes in the bottom and then it is recycled and made back in the ice again. So if you do not remove the ice as it is being made then it simply goes from water to ice to water to ice to water to ice and so on. Also, if you remove the ice and place it into the freezer, the ice will be “wet” so it will freeze together and you will need to break it apart to use it.

This is a nice ice machine, but you just have to make sure that your expectations meet what the machine will do.

This ice machine is made in China and being sold by Chinese company on Amazon.
